title: Past regional error quantiles raised high tide flood interval scores against pooled quantiles at 83 US gauges in 2022-2025
abstract: We tested whether past errors from the same coastal region improve later annual flood day ranges. We used a verified NOAA evidence table. Each test year used only earlier rows from 2019 onward. The test has 307 station-years at 83 US gauges in 2022-2025. We estimated signed error quantiles by region or across all gauges. The regional model raised the equal-year mean 68%-target interval score by 1.59 days. Lower scores are better. Scores rose in three of four years. Conditional station-and-year bootstrap limits for the score change were -0.17 to +3.53 days. Pooled mean score was 16.05 days for regional limits and 14.47 days for global limits. Coverage was 55.4% and 58.0%. Regional error structure in the full record did not give this simple correction a later-year gain. Only four test years, sparse regional samples, data revisions and shared coastal conditions limit the result. The test does not rule out other regional models or identify a physical cause. Code, all limits, source hashes, a separate arithmetic check and a figure are included.

display.caption: Past regional signed error quantiles gave higher mean interval scores than global quantiles in three of four test years. Limits use only earlier years. The dotted line marks the chosen 68% coverage target.

citations.reason: Verified derived table, threshold controls and prior regional error summary. Observations overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
